name: John Muir Trail
permitNote: JMT lottery via Recreation.gov. Yosemite-exit permits extremely competitive — apply 24 weeks in advance. Easier from Whitney Portal northbound.

name: Half Dome
permitNote: Preseason lottery in March. Daily lottery 2 days ahead during season. ~300 permits/day.

name: High Sierra Trail
location: Sequoia NP to Mt. Whitney, CA
permitNote: Reserve on Recreation.gov up to 6 months ahead. Quota season May 23 – Sep 27; $15 + $5/person. Competitive but more obtainable than JMT.

name: Mt. Whitney Summit
permitNote: February lottery on Recreation.gov. Overnight permits harder than day. ~60 overnight/day in season.

name: Big Pine Lakes
permitNote: Big Pine Creek North Fork permit via Recreation.gov. Sells out fast — book at 7am PT, 6 months ahead.

name: Thousand Island Lake Loop
permitNote: Inyo NF permit via Recreation.gov. Multiple trailhead options (Agnew Meadows easiest to score).

name: Minaret Lake
permitNote: Inyo NF wilderness permit, Devils Postpile trailhead quota. Moderate competition.

name: Pear Lake
permitNote: Sequoia wilderness permit via Recreation.gov. Lakes Trail quota — book 6 months out.

name: Lost Coast Trail
permitNote: Advance lottery via Recreation.gov (Oct for following year). Tide-dependent — plan around low tides or get stranded.

name: Yosemite Falls Trail
permitNote: Day hike needs no permit. Backcountry overnight requires Yosemite wilderness permit via Recreation.gov.

name: The Enchantments
permitNote: Core Enchantment Zone = hardest permit in the PNW. February lottery via Recreation.gov; <3% success. Day-hiking needs no permit.

name: Sahale Glacier Camp
permitNote: North Cascades backcountry permit. Early-access lottery April, but most permits are walk-up 1 day ahead at Wilderness Info Center. Only 4 sites at Sahale.

name: Wonderland Trail
permitNote: Early Access Lottery opens Feb 10, closes Mar 3. General permits from Apr 25. ~600 itineraries online + 300 walk-ups. 27,000 ft total gain.

name: Spider Gap–Buck Creek Pass Loop
permitNote: No permit required. Self-register at trailhead. Northwest Forest Pass for parking. Snow on Spider Glacier into August.

name: Diablo Lake / Ross Lake
permitNote: North Cascades backcountry permit. Boat-in sites on Ross Lake book separately via Ross Lake Resort (water taxi).

name: Jade Lake
permitNote: Self-register at trailhead, Northwest Forest Pass for parking. Off-trail scramble required — navigation skills essential.

name: Olympic Coast (South)
permitNote: Olympic wilderness permit via Recreation.gov. Tide tables mandatory. Bear canisters required. Less crowded than northern coast.

name: Hoh River Trail
permitNote: Olympic wilderness permit. Check closures — road damage has affected access. Rainforest — pack rain gear.

name: Mt. Hood Timberline Trail
permitNote: No permit required for backpacking. Northwest Forest Pass for parking. Sandy River and Eliot Branch crossings can be dangerous in afternoon — cross early.

name: Mt. Shasta (Avalanche Gulch)
permitNote: Self-issue climbing permit + summit pass ($25) at Bunny Flat trailhead. Requires ice axe, crampons, mountaineering skills.

name: Crater Lake Rim Area
permitNote: Free backcountry permit at visitor center day of or before. No camping within 1 mile of rim road.

name: Teton Crest Trail
permitNote: Early-access lottery January via Recreation.gov. Remaining permits walk-up day-of. Very competitive for Death Canyon Shelf zone.

name: Paintbrush–Cascade Canyon Loop
permitNote: Same Grand Teton permit system as Teton Crest. Paintbrush Divide often holds snow into late July.

name: Cirque of the Towers
permitNote: No permit required in Bridger-Teton / Shoshone NF. Free and wild. Remote trailhead — 90+ min dirt road access.

name: Sky Pond via Glacier Gorge
permitNote: RMNP timed-entry permit for park access (summer). Overnight needs wilderness permit. Class 4 scramble past Timberline Falls.

name: Weminuche / San Juans
permitNote: No permit required for most of the Weminuche. Chicago Basin accessed via Durango & Silverton train. 14er country.

name: Grand Canyon Rim-to-Rim
permitNote: Backcountry permit via Recreation.gov. Apply 4 months ahead (e.g. Jan 1 for May). Bright Angel/Phantom Ranch corridor most competitive. Avoid summer — lethal heat.

name: Havasu Falls
permitNote: Permits via havasupaireservations.com — release Feb 1 annually, sell out in minutes. ~$455/person for 3 nights. Tribal land, not NPS.

name: Paria Canyon
permitNote: BLM permit via Recreation.gov, 4 months ahead. Only 20 overnight permits/day. Check flash flood forecasts obsessively.

name: Coyote Gulch
permitNote: Free self-issue permit at trailhead kiosk. Multiple entry options (Hurricane Wash easiest, Crack-in-the-Wall most dramatic).

name: Zion Narrows (Top-Down)
permitNote: Zion wilderness permit via Recreation.gov. 3-month advance lottery + last-minute drawing 2 weeks out + walk-up. 40+ river crossings; drysuit in cold months.

name: Glacier NP — Highline/Gunsight
permitNote: Advance lottery March via Recreation.gov. Walk-up permits day-before at backcountry offices. Bear spray mandatory.

name: Arrigetch Peaks
location: Gates of the Arctic NP, AK
permitNote: No permits, no trails, no bridges. Fly-in only via bush plane from Bettles. Full wilderness skills + bear canister required.

name: Grewingk Glacier Lake
permitNote: No permit. $6/person park fee + water taxi fee from Homer. Dog-friendly. Easiest 'epic' trip on the list.

name: Presidential Traverse
permitNote: No permit. AMC huts require reservations months ahead ($$$). Camping restricted above treeline. Weather kills — check Mt. Washington forecast religiously.

name: Mt. LeConte via Alum Cave
permitNote: LeConte Lodge reservations release Oct 1 for following year (books fast). Backcountry shelter permit via Recreation.gov. Free park entry.

name: Roan Highlands (AT section)
permitNote: No permit required on this AT section. Carver's Gap to US 19E. Balds above treeline — exposed in storms.
